steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Sauté garlic in hot oil for 1 to 2 minutes. Add tomato sauce, salsa, chili powder, onion, parsley, basil, oregano, cumin, black pepper, and salt.
Stir in water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Red Enchilada Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This red enchilada sauce recipe features tomato sauce, garlic, onion, and salsa simmered with spices and herbs, including basil, cumin, and oregano.
raw_recipe.name: Red Enchilada Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Sauté garlic in hot oil for 1 to 2 minutes. Add tomato sauce, salsa, chili powder, onion, parsley, basil, oregano, cumin, black pepper, and salt.
Stir in water; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I am so glad I read the other reviews before I made this dish. This recipe makes an excellent enchilada sauce with a few changes: 1) use tomato paste instead of sauce 2) use chicken broth instead of water 3) blend the salsa to make it smooth 4) double the chili powder and 5) cook the sauce for several hours, adding broth to maintain a smooth consistency. I made this sauce with Gerry's Chicken Enchiladas, also on this site.

I used this for the Angela’s Enchiladas recipe and it turned out really well! However I would recommend using poultry stock (I used turkey) instead of water and letting it simmer for about 30 min, long enough so that it puckers on the surface. Delicious! Thank you for this recipe!

I have not had enchilada sauce for a long time. But this tasted good the way it was. I made a second batch (which I liked better, but you might not) and changed it a bit. I ADDED: A 6oz. CAN TOMATO PASTE, 1 1/2tsp smoked paprika, 1 tbsp brown sugar, USED ONLY 1 cup water with chicken bouillon mixed in.

I followed what several reviews had suggested and substituted 1 1/2 cups low sodium chicken broth for the water. I also let the mixture simmer for an additional 20 minutes for a total of 40 minutes and then used my infusion blender to make the mixture smooth. You can also use a blender. I also used a homemade fired roasted salsa. Sauce is yummy yummy yummy.

I made some significant alterations and doubled the recipe and followed many suggestions. I halved the pepper, added red pepper for the other half for a fuller mouth heat, upped the oregano and chilly pepper a bit, a dash or to of marjoram to round the flavor, traded the tomato sauce for tomato paste and water for chicken broth (I used a full container of chicken broth) and it helped with the constancy as I'd added more dry then called for, I also added handfuls of frozen corn. I used my homemade blender salsa. Then used 5 frozen chicken breasts ( I have a large family and wanted some left overs) and pressure cooked it in oregano olive oil (I make my own), Johnny Salt, Johnny Salt Garlic, Taco seasoning, cumin and salt and cooked my chicken for 20 min and then shredded it. I then poured 1/2 my sauce in with my chicken, spooned my chicken into my flour tortillas, a handful of a nice shredded Mexican blend of cheese, rolled them width wise in my lasagna pan, nine deep and poured sauce over the top and then covered with cheeses and cooked at 350 for 30 min. I made a second pan to save for latter... Half the children were gone. My husband said it was the best enchiladas he had ever had. My son agreed. They were tired and hungry but they did turn out beautiful. I recommend making sure to enjoy the taste and constancy of your sauce before for your best results. :)

I skipped the sautée step and omitted the oil Sauce was all I had on hand so I used a standard sized can and just enough water to rinse out the can. To this water, I added a small splash of liquid Au jus concentrate. I omitted the "Italian"- type seasonings. Had I any oregano, I would have used some; ditto cocoa or baking chocolate. For spices I used two or three heaping teaspoons of chili powder and an equal amount of ground cumin, one or two heaping teaspoons of onion powder, a heaping teaspoon of dry minced garlic, some chili-lime salt- a good few shakes, some white pepper, a dash of cinnamon and salted with garlic salt. I used a three-ounce individual snack-size cup of salsa because I had it on hand and perhaps an 8th of a cup of my "special" salsa (purchased from a Cuban restaurant on my birthday) for it's distinctive smoky flavor. Following the suggestions of previous reviewers, I used my stick blender for a smooth texture and added a bay leaf to the mix- which was really quite thick, after transferring to a covered small saucepan over medium low heat. I also added a scant teaspoon of turbinado sugar after everything was in the pan and cooking to sort of soften the taste of all of the spices. If it's still too strongly spiced, I will probably add a second can of sauce. Made sauce to accompany crockpot enchilada casserole. I think that this recipe is a good jumping off point for experimentation. Will likely make again and continue tinkering.

I made modifications as suggested by substitute tomato paste and chicken broth for the sauce and water. I simmered it for an hour. I doubled the recipe so I would have enough since some said it didn’t make enough sause. I also added a can of Roten tomatoes instead of the salsa. I will definitely make this again since my husband loved it as did my dinner guests.

This recipe exceeded my expectations! My super picky 8 year old raved about it. I did add however a couple of generous spoonfuls of cream cheese and simmered it to add some thickness and creaminess and let it simmer longer than the recipe suggests. This is definitely being added to our meal rotation ! I didn't find any Italian taste as the previous reviews suggest.

After reading the reviews from others, I doubled the chili powder, left out the oregano, added a chopped up fresh tomato, tripled the chopped onion, added a small can ofdiced green chilies, and replaced the salt with a double measurement of onion salt. I used a crock pot: on high until the sauce bubbled, then turned it down to low for several hours. It is quite spicy (tossed left over hot picante and hot salsa in, about 1/4 cup each). It DOES taste like enchilada sauce. It is just about as hot as I can tolerate, although my partner eats food much hotter than this. It complements the black olives that I use to bake the enchiladas. Next time I will use tomato paste instead of sauce, as it turned out just a teensy bit runnier that would be optimal.

As per the very first review, i also used tomato paste, and chicken stock. After sauteing the onion and garlic, I put it all in the slowcooker for a couple hours. It was my first time making enchiladas, and my husband graciously left me one whole enchilada out of the entire pan! Best compliment I could get from him! Thank you!
This sauce is delicious. I blended coriander, a couple of chipotles, chix bouillon and a can of diced tomatoes w/onion, oregano and basil to use as the salsa. This is a keeper.
I did not have any salsa so I used Rotelle tomatoes. Had to make my own sauce tomato sauce diced tomatoes but it turned out great
Only did not have a 6oz can of tomato sauce; used 11oz can and light on the chili powder as family prefers mild. Have made it many times!
I made a triple batch for my 3 pans of enchiladas. I added 2 cans of tomato paste but now I'm not sure they were necessary. I'll use this recipe again but probably without the pre-prepared salsa.
I added a can of tomato paste to thicken it up some, but otherwise followed the directions right down the line
Omitted salsa, added just a hint of brown sugar, and sprinkles of paprika. Scaled back water. Great!
I love this recipe. I always double/triple it with very predictable results. One recommendation: Less water to suit your taste.
Thought I had a can. So I went to this recipe and it did was exactly perfect! Thanks so much for keeping my dinner on track!!!

I liked this recipe a lot, and I will definitely be using it again. I used the immersion blender to smooth it out as I used a can of diced tomatoes and wanted a smoother sauce, and I replaced the cumin as we cannot use it in our house. The only addition I made to the recipe other than that was to add some red pepper paste as a bit of a thickener.
Best ever!!!! Tried what feels like hundreds of sauces. Not too heavy - perfect! This one is by far our favorite and will be the one we use FOREVER!
